title: A Crown for the Veil
premise: Mara Joubert has spent six years swallowing poison for King Aldric, building immunity one dish at a time while memorizing every smuggler's road through the Thornfell mountains. When a dying courier presses a map into her hands—a map showing the thirteenth moon's path to a shrine where the Veil, an ancient entity, was bound into the royal crown—Mara discovers the king she serves died years ago and the thing wearing his crown has been slowly consuming the court. Hunted by the Veil's enforcers and betrayed by the spymaster who raised her, Mara must ally with Prince Caelan, the exiled heir whose blood alone can unbind his father. In the end, Mara reaches the shrine as the thirteenth moon rises and offers her own poisoned-immune blood alongside Caelan's, shattering the crown; Caelan takes a throne he never wanted while Mara walks free of both duty and crown, choosing him over the kingdom that used them both.
about_author: Sable Kavanagh is a former line cook from a mountain town who swears her years in professional kitchens taught her everything she knows about poison, politics, and patience. She writes fantasy about ordinary people caught in extraordinary machinery, usually late at night, usually with too much coffee.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Mara. During a state banquet, Mara tastes a subtly wrong dish and saves three nobles' lives, earning the Veiled King's unsettling attention—he watches her with eyes that don't blink enough. The emotional beat: pride curdling into dread as she realizes her skill has made her visible to something that shouldn't notice anyone.

chapters.title: Blood on the Thornfell Road
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Traveling her usual smuggler route to source rare spices, Mara finds a courier dying of wounds no blade makes—his flesh smoking like embers. He presses a leather map tube into her hands and gasps: 'Thirteen turns. The shrine. Unbind him.' The beat: terror and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Hiding in a smuggler's den, Mara deciphers the map: it charts not roads but the moon's path across thirteen months, ending at a mountain shrine, annotated with the words 'the crown is the cage.' She recognizes the seal of Prince Caelan, exiled seven years ago. The beat: dawning horror reframing everything she knows.

chapters.title: The Court That Smiles Too Much
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Back at the palace, Mara notices what she'd trained herself not to see: servants with hollow eyes, nobles repeating phrases verbatim, the king never eating. Her mentor, Spymaster Vess, questions her too gently about her trip. The beat: paranoia blooming—the palace is a body being eaten from inside.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Summoned privately, the king speaks to her in two voices—one pleading for help, one silkily threatening. The human fragment inside begs her to find Caelan before the thirteenth turn. The Veil lets her leave, curious what she'll do. The beat: compassion for the prisoner inside her captor.

chapters.title: The Exile's Price
chapters.summary: POV Caelan. In a border town, disgraced prince Caelan drinks away his exile until Mara finds him. He refuses: his father banished him cruelly, and he owes the crown nothing. Mara shows him the map—and the second voice's message. The beat: bitter grief meeting stubborn hope.

chapters.title: Vess's Web
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Vess reveals she's known about the Veil for years and has been feeding it small treasons to keep the court 'stable.' She orders Mara to surrender the map. Mara flees instead, stealing palace keys. The beat: betrayal by the only mother figure she had.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads
chapters.summary: POV Mara and Caelan alternating. Fleeing through Thornfell using Mara's smuggler knowledge, pursued by enforcers whose shadows move wrong. They argue about duty versus survival, and Caelan begins to see his father's true fate. The beat: grudging partnership kindling into trust.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Caelan. A village on their route has no memories older than seven years—the Veil's reach extends beyond the palace. An old woman recognizes Caelan's face and weeps without knowing why. The beat: the scale of the horror becomes personal.

chapters.title: Poison and Antidote
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Ambushed at a river crossing, Mara survives because six years of microdoses have made her blood toxic to the Veil's touch—it recoils from her. Caelan realizes her 'curse' of a profession is the weapon they need. The beat: her suffering reframed as power.

chapters.title: The Shrine's First Door
chapters.summary: POV Mara. They reach the outer shrine, sealed by royal blood. Caelan cuts his palm; the door opens onto trials left by the last binders—tests of memory, sacrifice, and truth. The first trial forces Caelan to relive his father's real last words: love, not rejection. The beat: grief transformed.

chapters.title: Turn Twelve
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The twelfth moon wanes. Vess catches up with an army of the hollow-eyed, offering Mara pardon if she abandons Caelan. Mara refuses; Vess hesitates, and something almost human flickers in her—she was consumed long ago. The beat: pity for the enemy, resolve hardened.

chapters.title: What the Veil Wants
chapters.summary: POV Caelan. Through dreams, the Veil tempts Caelan: his father's throne, his father's love, everything restored if he simply stops fighting. It shows him Mara dying in a hundred futures. The beat: temptation that costs him sleepless honesty with Mara about his fear.

chapters.title: Confessions at the Fire
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A quiet night before the final ascent. Mara tells Caelan how she became a taster—an orphan sold to the palace, poisoning herself so no one else would die. He tells her he ran because he couldn't bear watching his father fade. The beat: love admitted quietly, against all sense.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Captured and returned to the palace as leverage, Mara witnesses the full horror: the entire court standing motionless at midnight, faces upturned toward the crown. The Veil offers her a bargain—her freedom for Caelan's surrender. The beat: despair at the machinery of power, then defiance.

chapters.title: Escape from the Gilded Cage
chapters.summary: POV Caelan. Caelan surrenders himself to save Mara, but she's already escaped using the smuggler tunnels beneath the kitchens—her old knowledge turned to war. She frees him mid-transfer ritual, and the human voice in the king screams 'run.' The beat: agency reclaimed, racing against the moon.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: POV Mara and Caelan. The final moonrise approaches as they climb to the inner shrine, Vess and the hollow court behind them, the Veil tearing free of its weakening cage ahead of schedule. The mountain itself groans. The beat: desperate urgency, no plan left but each other.

chapters.title: Trials of Blood and Memory
chapters.summary: POV Caelan. The inner trials demand more than royal blood: Caelan must surrender his claim to the throne entirely, and Mara must offer her immune blood willingly, knowing it may kill her. They speak vows—not marriage, but choice. The beat: love against duty, made literal.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Mara. At the altar, their mingled blood strikes the crown. The Veil erupts from its cage, offering Mara everything—power, safety, Vess restored—if she stops. She answers with the one thing it cannot consume: a self built from swallowed poison. The crown shatters. The beat: climax, identity as weapon.

chapters.title: The King Who Died
chapters.summary: POV Caelan. The Veil unravels, releasing the court—and the true King Aldric's spirit, held seven years past death, finally thanks his son and lets go. Vess wakes, broken and grieving for her lost decades. The beat: mourning and mercy intertwined.

chapters.title: A Reluctant Coronation
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Caelan is crowned with no crown at all—a circlet of plain iron, by his own decree, so nothing can be bound to it again. He asks Mara to stay not as taster but as equal. The court rebuilds; Vess takes quiet penance. The beat: cautious hope, power consciously limited.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Thornfell
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Epilogue. Mara chooses neither throne nor tower: she and Caelan ride the smuggler roads together, mapping a kingdom that will know its own paths honestly this time. She carries the shattered crown's last shard as a reminder. The beat: freedom chosen, love kept, identity whole.
